id: Darren Watson Plays The Shed-The Shed, 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 50, Lower Hutt-Event Finder
name: Darren Watson Plays The Shed
venue: The Shed, 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 50, Lower Hutt
long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

id: Natural Textured Rings for Christmas - Taster Class-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Natural Textured Rings for Christmas - Taster Class
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

venue: Cobblestones Heritage Village, 169 Main Street, Greytown
long_description:
Unsung Heroes, Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley, with special guests Kate Marshall and Angela Fox.
They sing, they play, they recount stories based on actual people and real events that occurred in our colonial history.
You'll enjoy their eclectic brand of folk heritage to in the very appropriate setting of Cobblestones Heritage Village.
You can expect to hear stories from Aotearoa New Zealand’s distant past in song, with newspaper clippings and poems as an introduction and a slideshow of historic images to accompany each tale.
The duo brings alive the incredible stories of our rogues, rebels and folk heroes in an entertaining history lesson through what music critic Marty Duda has called Priestley’s beautiful melodies and “a wonderful, simple, direct singing style.”
They are stories about us, this place and people we hadn’t heard of, wrote another reviewer, Mike Mizrahi.
“Helping to create the wonderful tapestry, unique in the world, of Aotearoa and the brave folk that came and settled here. It was driven by immediate, moving and wonderfully fashioned songs that told these great tales, accompanied by incredible slide imagery that transported audiences to these times.”
The duo are accomplished musicians, whether individually or appearing in a multitude of different groups or collaborative ventures. For this concert they will be joined by local multi-instrumentalist Kate Marshall and will be bringing a few local stories.
Unsung Heroes have performed as part of the Auckland Heritage Festival, and in Christchurch, Wellington and Dunedin but also taken their brand of folk history through folk music to the likes of Gore, Katikati, Inglewood, Okarito, St Bathans and other small locales – and now they are excited to bring this performance to Cobblestones.
Seating is limited and tickets are $25 cash on the door with bookings by text to 02102361951 or buy through Eventfinda

Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live. Secure your tickets early and don't miss the opportunity to see true pioneers of alternative hip hop when they return this December.

long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Art Clay Silver is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of small charms.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

long_description:
Create gorgeous simple leadlight suncatchers with Lisa Sinclair!

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

More experienced students may bring existing projects to work on in class - though emphasis will be placed on focusing on the same techniques of flat, nicely soldered simple designs.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.
Additional materials and tools are available to purchase.

Not suitable for children. Older teenagers (16+) are welcome.
